page: Microsoft Azure E96-48as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance within the Easv7 family, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor on the x86_64 architecture, providing 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores running at up to 4.5 GHz. It is configured with 768 GB of memory, yielding a 16 GB memory-per-core ratio. The underlying CPU supports AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, hardware virtualization via SVM, and hardware cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not bundle local disk storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Performance testing shows top-tier execution across single-threaded and memory-bound tasks. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2878.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3790.57. Memory subsystem performance is strong, recording a PassMark memory score of 2985.6, cached memory read bandwidth of 5101.4 GB/sec, and uncached write bandwidth of 100.69 GB/sec. In multi-core throughput, the system produced a Geekbench multi-core score of 25354.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 79838.97. Application benchmarks reflect 78.4 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 400.89 tokens per second for small-model text generation.

With its constrained vCPU configuration on a 96-core platform footprint, the E96-48as_v7 provides qualitative cost efficiency for environments constrained by per-core software licensing models. Users gain access to 768 GB of memory without paying licensing fees on unused cores. A key technical tradeoff is the absence of local storage, necessitating reliance on remote network-attached disks for persistent data. This hardware profile is well suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, and high-footprint analytical workloads.

The instance incorporates AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions, has no integrated local storage, and contains zero GPUs. Benchmark measurements reflect top-tier single-core and memory results, including a Geekbench single-core score of 2878.0, a PassMark memory score of 2985.6, and Redis throughput of 78.4 million SET operations per second.
